title: The Nvidia Machine Is Self-Sustaining – And Was Already Facing A Tougher Future

The Nvidia Machine Is Self-Sustaining – And Was Already Facing A Tougher Future

Timothy Prickett Morgan

Timothy Prickett
Morgan

Co-Editor, Co-Founder, The Next Platform

Published
thu 12 Nov 2026 // 18:42 UTC

Well, like most of you on Earth, I didn’t see that coming.The third and most important of the co-founders of Nvidia, Jensen Huang, has resigned as president and chief executive officer and Colette Kress, the longtime chief financial officer of the company, has been tapped as his interim replacement in the wake of the revelation of two affairs by Huang – one with an executive at Singaporean company Megaspeed International (who may be a Chinese government operative) and another with an executive in the top ranks at Nvidia itself.

NEXTPLATFORM AD

There is a lot of chatter that Megaspeed was channeling either Nvidia-based GPU systems or remote access to them (or both) to Chinese companies, including upstart model maker DeepSeek, and it is not clear if Huang knew this when a sister company of Megaspeed bought $4.8 billion in Nvidia GPU gear between June 2024 and February 2026. The Information is reporting that Megaspeed and its affiliates have acquired $7.5 billion in GPU systems since 2023. The US Commerce Department had been investigating Megaspeed since late 2024, according to the timeline put together by the New York Times, but those investigations apparently stalled as President Trump and Jensen Huang started getting chummy last year. The investigations were moved over to the US Department of Justice, and it is unclear what state they are in.Suffice it to say, the new Congress being sworn in coming January 2027 will be all over this issue, and eventually facts will be gathered and punishments will be meted out as appropriate – and a presidential pardon for Jensen Huang should he be indicted for being complicit in the smuggling of systems made by Inspur into China or the renting of capacity on systems to Megaspeed customers like Alibaba.It is not clear that the latter is yet illegal, but if you are putting export controls on physical machines, it only makes sense that you should have export controls on selling capacity from a cloud over the wires. In any event, Alibaba obviously builds its own AI models and would benefit from having access to Nvidia GPUs that are under export controls and are forbidden to be sold to organizations in China. It is also not clear where Megaspeed got its money to buy GPU systems and to build datacenters in Indonesia and China, but it is reasonable to infer that it stretches back into China.Let the chips fall where they may.

NEXTPLATFORM AD

For now, Harvey Jones, who was once chief executive officer at chip design software maker Synopsis and who is a managing partner with venture capitalist Square Wave Ventures, has been tapped as chairman of the board. This is the first time Nvidia has had a chairman. Jones has been on the board of Nvidia since November 1993, shortly after the company was founded in April 1993. The board is starting a CEO search to replace Huang and Kress, and there is every reason to believe that Kress will continue in her role as CFO in the wake of the new CEO coming in.Aside from all of these issues, the biggest one is how the AI industry and Nvidia within it will work without Jensen Huang in the middle of it, being the ambassador for the AI future as well as its biggest beneficiary of the GenAI revolution that no company has capitalized on better than Nvidia. (That revolution has made Huang the 15th richest person in the world, with $145 billion of Nvidia stock ahead of the affair revelations earlier this week.) Huang has to give up $108 million in share compensation by stepping down, and his 3.6 percent stake in Nvidia is also taking some lumps, but he will have plenty of capital to start something new if he so desires to do so. It seems likely that Huang will try to lay low for a while, and try to heal his relationships with his wife and children. The world will likely not let him lay low.As for Nvidia, Huang is famous for running a tight ship and for having the company’s 60 top executives directly report to him so he knew exactly what everyone was doing and why. The good news for Nvidia is that this process is in place, and each of these five dozen executives are well acquainted with their jobs. Moreover, the Nvidia AI system roadmaps are set for the “Rubin” and “Feynman” generations of GPUs that will carry the company into 2030, and Nvidia’s production is sold out for 2027 already and it won’t be long before it is sold out for 2028 if history and increasing demand is any guide. If there was a time where Nvidia can largely run itself, it is now.That said, Nvidia has never faced so many pressures from so many different forces at the same time.

NEXTPLATFORM AD

The hyperscalers, cloud builders, and AI model builders are all working on their own custom CPUs and XPU AI accelerators to not only wean themselves off of very expensive Nvidia iron and to create hardware specifically to run their own AI models for around half of what it costs to do it with the Nvidia hardware and systems software stack.Moreover, Nvidia is championing open source and open weight AI models – something only Nvidia can afford to do because it gets such a high premium for its AI compute and networking hardware. These open Nemotron models directly compete against the closed source and usually closed weight models of its largest GPU accelerator customers, which probably has them irked a bit.But even more alarming for those who have enjoyed the meteoric rise of Nvidia during the GenAI boom, it is not clear that the rosy forecasts for AI spending out in 2029 and 2030 and beyond can be met because of supply chain constraints for many components as well as the difficulty of adding more electricity capacity to the grids of the world.And in America at least, there is rising dissatisfaction for what is perceived of as preferential treatment that datacenter operators have enjoyed for the past decade and a half. It is not a coincidence that residential electric bills have gone up as datacenters have proliferated, and people are annoyed by the elitist attitudes of the tech titans who control AI. They are also rightly concerned with what GenAI will do to the economies, societies, and cultures of the world.

NEXTPLATFORM AD

Finally, by Huang exiting the top job at Nvidia, the AI industry just got a lot less coherent and eloquent. And now we will find out just how important Huang would have been in a future that was already much less certain for Nvidia before he was compelled to leave the company.
